tasks.title: Add --pods N flag to sessions.py and auth-storm.py for multi-pod distributed load generation
tasks.accept: python3 -c "import ast, sys; tree=ast.parse(open('benchmarks/campus35k/sessions.py').read()); args=[a.arg for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and node.name=='main' for a in node.args.args]; assert 'pods' in args or any('pods' in str(a) for a in ast.walk(tree)), 'sessions.py missing pods parameter'; tree2=ast.parse(open('benchmarks/campus35k/auth-storm.py').read()); args2=[a.arg for node in ast.walk(tree2) if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and node.name=='main' for a in node.args.args]; assert 'pods' in args2 or any('pods' in str(a) for a in ast.walk(tree2)), 'auth-storm.py missing pods parameter'"
tasks.acceptance_prose:
You work in an isolated git worktree of /home/weissto_local/git/next-mailserver.

CONTEXT: benchmarks/campus35k/sessions.py and auth-storm.py currently run from a single pod. The arc42 risk 'Single-pod load generator saturates at C=200' documents that the load generator itself becomes the bottleneck at C=200 (achieved only 175.5/200 mean concurrency). A multi-pod generator (≥2 pods) is needed before probing >200 concurrent. The scripts already support --concurrency, --duration, --domain, --user-range flags.

TASK:
1. In benchmarks/campus35k/sessions.py:
   a) Add a `--pods N` command-line argument (default 1). When N > 1, the script should either: (i) print instructions for running N pods (kubectl run with the script as a configmap), OR (ii) actually launch N kubectl run pods that each run the script with --concurrency split across pods. Option (i) is simpler and safer for a first implementation.
   b) When --pods N is specified, print a message like: 'To run with N pods, execute: kubectl run sessions-load-{i} --image=python:3-slim --restart=Never --command -- python3 /opt/sessions.py --concurrency C/N --duration D --domain DOMAIN' for each pod.
   c) Add a `parse_pods(spec)` helper function that parses the --pods argument (similar to existing parse_user_range).
   d) Do NOT break existing behavior when --pods is not specified (default 1).
2. In benchmarks/campus35k/auth-storm.py:
   a) Same changes: add `--pods N` argument, `parse_pods()` helper, and multi-pod launch instructions.
3. Commit with message: 'feat(bench): multi-pod load generator (--pods N) for sessions.py and auth-storm.py'

GATE: `python3 -c "import ast; tree=ast.parse(open('benchmarks/campus35k/sessions.py').read()); args=[a.arg for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and node.name=='main' for a in node.args.args]; assert 'pods' in args or any('pods' in str(a) for a in ast.walk(tree)), 'sessions.py missing pods parameter'; tree2=ast.parse(open('benchmarks/campus35k/auth-storm.py').read()); args2=[a.arg for node in ast.walk(tree2) if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and node.name=='main' for a in node.args.args]; assert 'pods' in args2 or any('pods' in str(a) for a in ast.walk(tree2)), 'auth-storm.py missing pods parameter'"`

tasks.title: Fix remaining F841 unused variables in test_idle_notification.py and code quality cleanup
tasks.accept: ruff check tests/integration/stalwart/test_idle_notification.py --select F841 2>&1 | grep -q 'All checks passed' || ruff check tests/integration/stalwart/test_idle_notification.py --select F841 2>&1 | wc -l | grep -q '^0$'
tasks.acceptance_prose:
You work in an isolated git worktree of /home/weissto_local/git/next-mailserver.

CONTEXT: tests/integration/stalwart/test_idle_notification.py has F841 unused variable warnings at lines 277 and 286 (initial_count, notification_count). These are pre-existing and were identified during the bug hunt round 2. The variables are assigned but never used in assertions.

TASK:
1. Run `ruff check tests/integration/stalwart/test_idle_notification.py --select F841` to identify all F841 warnings.
2. For each F841 warning, either:
   a) Use the variable in an assertion (preferred — the variable was probably meant to be checked), OR
   b) Rename to `_` (if the variable is intentionally unused, e.g., a function return value that's part of an API contract), OR
   c) Remove the assignment entirely if the function call has no side effects.
3. For `initial_count` (line ~277): this is likely the count before an IDLE operation. It should be used in an assertion like `assert initial_count >= 0` or compared with the post-IDLE count.
4. For `notification_count` (line ~286): this is likely the count of IDLE notifications received. It should be used in an assertion like `assert notification_count >= 0` or `assert notification_count == expected`.
5. Do NOT change any other file. Do NOT remove tests or change test logic — only fix the unused variable warnings.
6. Commit with message: 'fix(tests): F841 unused variables in test_idle_notification.py (initial_count, notification_count)'

GATE: `ruff check tests/integration/stalwart/test_idle_notification.py --select F841` must report zero F841 warnings.
